scenes.headline: Pruning SuperPoint where the time really is
scenes.sub: A faster keypoint front-end for edge devices
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bracken! SuperPoint finds interest points in an image. This version runs faster on a tiny robot board.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Cut whole channels out of the convolutions that run at full resolution, then train a small student to behave like the original.
scenes.say: The trick: the first layers see every pixel, so they cost the most. Shrink those, then repair the damage with a teacher.

steps.say: An image enters one shared encoder, a stack of eight small convolutions.
It splits into two heads: one scores interest points, the other emits descriptors for matching.
Pruning happens here, in the first convolutions that run at full resolution.
That hurts quality, so the original model teaches the smaller student to copy it.

left.title: Zero the weights
left.say: Zeroing individual weights keeps the layer's shape, so a dense convolution still runs full size. No faster.

right.title: Remove channels
right.say: Removing whole channels makes the layer smaller and the convolution genuinely quicker.

scenes.title: Inference time at full HD, lower is better
scenes.say: At full HD a frame drops from about one hundred eleven milliseconds to fifty-four. That is the headline speedup.

scenes.title: Keypoints covered, out of 1024
scenes.say: Prune one layer untrained and coverage falls to six hundred thirty-seven. Prune six and distill: back to eight hundred seventeen.

scenes.text: Compute fell over three times, but latency only about two: the heads and keypoint selection never shrink.
scenes.say: So the lesson is honest. The front layers win real time, but the heads, the suppression and the selection set a floor.
Prune where the pixels are, distill to recover, and keep the interface. That is the whole trick.
